notable_absence.finding: 'If you want to support both HTTP and HTTPS connections you will need to run two separate instances of Sync Gateway.' - a single Sync Gateway instance cannot serve plain HTTP and HTTPS side by side; this is a genuine mutual-exclusion fact but modelling it cleanly would require minting distinct 'HTTP-only mode'/'HTTPS-only mode' concepts for what the page treats as a single boolean (SSLCert/SSLKey present or absent), so it is left as a finding rather than forced into mutuallyExclusiveWith's symmetric two-concept shape.

cross_component_finding: This page is the clearest evidence yet that Sync Gateway's connection-TO-Couchbase-Server X.509 setup is not a parallel, Sync-Gateway-specific PKI surface but a direct consumer of Server's own certificate machinery: both prerequisite steps ('Create a Root and Node Certificates', 'Enable Client Certificate Authentication') link straight into server/current/manage/manage-security/ pages, and the resulting client certificate is explicitly 'signed by the root certificate' from that same Server-side procedure. This is the opposite finding from the client-facing SSLCert/SSLKey TLS surface earlier on the same page, which is entirely Sync-Gateway's own (no link into server/ at all) - the page cleanly separates 'Sync Gateway is a TLS server to its clients' (own surface, sgw:tls-client-connection) from 'Sync Gateway is a certificate-bearing client of Couchbase Server' (reused surface, cert:client-certificate/cert:root-certificate) within a single page.
cross_product_finding: auth-mechanism:x509-certificate and the cert:* family, both previously seen only in server/'s own certificate docs, recur here in a second product's page with the *same* identity - this page's own cross-references into server/current/manage/manage-security/configure-server-certificates.md and configure-client-certificates.md are the direct textual evidence that Sync Gateway's Server-connection cert auth is not a new mechanism but literal reuse of Server's PKI, which is why this batch reuses cert:root-certificate/cert:node-certificate/cert:client-certificate/cert:trust-store/auth-mechanism:x509-certificate rather than minting sgw:-prefixed parallels for this particular surface - unlike the client-facing TLS surface (sgw:tls-client-connection), which stays its own concept because no equivalent cross-reference into server/'s docs exists for it.
